assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling made aryl amines accessible by a straightforward, general catalytic route and is now routine in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. It is the kind of simple, broadly consequential method I value, and it fits the tradition begun by the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled catalytic methodology and the mechanistic understanding. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor with a real priority claim, but the general catalytic method is credited to the other two, and a three-person prize is possible.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of use, with extensive independent confirmation and industrial adoption. Recognition is more than timely.
uncertainties: How much weight Kosugi's 1983 precedent deserves versus the later general catalytic systems.
Whether the committee sees this as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize; I am working from memory on the details of that precedent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry that made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable, including the mRNA vaccines. This is a game-changer with enormous demonstrated consequences, and the design of pH-responsive lipids is a molecular-level chemical advance.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Madden, Hope, MacLachlan) built the foundational lipid-nanoparticle and ionizable-lipid technology, while Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoid and screening approaches. Credit is spread over many people and companies, so one to three laureates is a hard cut.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale, with years of independent confirmation. Timely, although the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside modification covers adjacent ground.
uncertainties: Who is decisive among Cullis, Madden, MacLachlan, Hope, Anderson and Langer, which I cannot settle from the supplied text.
Whether the discovery is more pharmaceutical than chemical in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base into another without double-strand breaks, a new chemical capability applied to the genome. It is a conceptual and practical game-changer, with first clinical successes.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory (Komor, Gaudelli as lead researchers) provided the cytosine and adenine base editors; Nishida and Kondo's Target-AID is an independent contemporaneous CBE. David Liu alone is the clearest decisive contributor, and prime editing (B057) would add to a single-laureate case.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials and therapies are emerging, so maturity is growing but not complete. Independent replication is broad in research use.
uncertainties: Whether Nishida and Kondo should share credit for the cytosine editor.
Whether long-term clinical safety and efficacy are established enough for the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets cells incorporate designed chemical groups into proteins in vivo. It is a new capability with consequences across protein engineering and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz, with Wang, established the first general in vivo methods; Chin extended it to multiple codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Yokoyama and Mehl are real contributors, so the three-person cut leaves out meaningful credit.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of use, with wide independent adoption. Mature.
uncertainties: The allocation among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Yokoyama and Mehl is unclear.
Practical impact outside specialist laboratories is more limited than for the top candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials give near quantum accuracy at force-field cost for large systems. This is a theory-and-simulation advance that has changed how materials and molecules are modelled, within my own field, and it ties quantitatively to experiment and ab initio data.
assessment.attribution: The Behler-Parrinello neural-network potential (2007) opened the field and the Csányi group's Gaussian approximation potentials followed. Bartók, von Lilienfeld and E also made major contributions, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Adoption is rapid, but the methods are still evolving, with foundation models arriving. Recognition may be early, and transferability is still debated.
uncertainties: Whether the field has stabilized enough for a prize.
Credit is split among at least six names; I may be biased toward simulation work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation recruits E3 ligases to destroy proteins chemically, a new pharmacological principle with clinical-stage drugs. It is a real game-changer for drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept and Ciulli supplied the structural and VHL-ligand chemistry. Handa, Ito and others uncovered cereblon as the thalidomide target, which is a separate molecular-glue line and complicates a compound prize.
assessment.maturity: Several drugs are in late-stage trials but none is approved, so clinical validation is incomplete and recognition may be a few years early.
uncertainties: The PROTAC and molecular-glue strands may need separate credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Descriptor-based computational design of catalysts, built on d-band and adsorption-energy scaling, turned theory into a predictive tool tied quantitatively to experiments in catalysis and electrochemistry. It meets my standard that theory must connect to measurement.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the clearest leader of the approach. Rossmeisl, Mavrikakis, Scheffler and Jaramillo made significant but more derivative or experimental contributions, and I would not add them from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and validation, with many predicted catalysts confirmed. Mature, although computational design has yet to yield a transformative commercial catalyst.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees it as the right mix of discovery and impact.
Hammer's role is not within the supplied credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates through liquid-liquid phase separation changed how cellular organization is understood and brought physical chemistry into cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne reported the P granule liquid-like behaviour in 2009, but Rosen, Pappu and Mittag provided essential physical and molecular principles. Allocation of credit is hard.
assessment.maturity: The concept is still debated in terms of generality and mechanism, so it may be premature, and chemistry versus biology placement is uncertain.
uncertainties: Disputes over in vivo relevance and the rigour of phase-separation criteria.
Whether this belongs in Chemistry or Medicine/Physiology.
